svg.title: Severe bleeding immediate-action card
svg.desc: A working Australian first-aid review card. Treat heavy bleeding, major traumatic bleeding, bleeding that firm pressure does not control, or bleeding with serious deterioration as life threatening. Call Triple Zero, put firm continuous pressure on the bleeding point, use one or two accurately placed pads rather than a loose stack, do not remove an embedded object, and keep watching the person. Separate kit and no-kit options are shown. Tourniquet and haemostatic-dressing mechanics are withheld for trained use with an exact product.
svg.text: Severe bleeding:
press now, call 000, keep pressing
WARNING — WORKING REVIEW CARD
Subjective estimates: core wording 95%; untested layout 72%.
These are not safety, success or survival probabilities.
This card cannot verify pressure or teach a tourniquet, wound
packing or haemostatic dressing. Follow 000 and exact training.
Australian clinical, practical and stressed-reader review is outstanding.
1 TREAT IT AS LIFE THREATENING IF ANY APPLY
• blood is heavy, spurting or rapidly soaking material
• there is an amputation or other major traumatic wound
• firm pressure is not controlling the bleeding
• the person is pale, sweaty, faint, confused or less responsive
CALL 000 NOW — do not wait for every sign
Use speaker. Have a helper call while pressure continues, if possible.
2 FIND THE BLEEDING POINT AND PRESS NOW
Check danger. Use gloves if they are ready; do not delay pressure.
Help the person lie down when breathing and injuries permit.
Expose only enough to find the point. Press firmly and continuously.
Use hands or a pad directly over the point. A helper or the injured
person may press. Do not keep lifting the pad to look.
KEEP PRESSURE ON THE POINT
3 USE THE RIGHT PRESSURE BRANCH
OPEN WOUND
Press directly on the bleeding point.
Keep the pressure firm and still.
PRESS ON THE POINT
OBJECT STUCK IN WOUND
Do not pull it out or press on it.
Press and pad around its sides.
PRESS AROUND — NOT ON
Eye or torso object: follow 000.
This card does not teach that care.
4 USE WHAT IS READY — DO NOT DELAY
WITH A FIRST-AID KIT
Use gloves if immediately ready.
Put a trauma pad or dressing over
the bleeding point and keep firm
continuous hand pressure on it.
WITHOUT A FIRST-AID KIT
Use clean, dry folded cloth or clothing.
If nothing is ready, hand pressure is
better than delay. Avoid blood contact
where possible.
5 IF BLOOD KEEPS COMING THROUGH
• keep pressure on the exact bleeding point
• add one second pad and a tighter bandage if available
• if still uncontrolled, check that the pads are on the point
• use firmer, focused pressure; do not build a loose stack
• tell 000 that bleeding remains uncontrolled
When controlled, secure the pad firmly without losing its position.
Keep watching for renewed bleeding.
6 UNCONTROLLED LIFE-THREATENING BLEEDING
Keep focused pressure and follow the 000 call-taker.
A manufactured arterial tourniquet is for life-threatening limb
bleeding not controlled by pressure — only with the exact product
and training. Haemostatic dressings also require training and an
exact product. This card gives no application or packing method.
Do not use a blood-draw band, narrow cord or wire. ANZCOR notes
that a failed improvised tourniquet can increase bleeding.
If trained and equipped, follow training/device instructions; record
the time, keep it visible and do not remove it in the field.
7 WHILE HELP IS COMING
Keep the person still, warm and observed. Recheck response, normal
breathing and the dressing. If bleeding returns, press again.
Give no food, drink or medicine. Record what happened and when.
If unresponsive and not breathing normally, use the CPR card and 000.
DO NOT: elevate · clean first · remove an object
Do not confuse wound pressure with snakebite pressure immobilisation.
WORKING DRAFT — Australian clinical, practical and stressed-reader review outstanding
